subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: In astronomical observations, signals observed from the distant stars are generally weak. If the photon detector receives a total of \(3.15 \times 10^{-18}\,\text{J}\) from the radiations of 600 nm, calculate the number of photons received by the detector.

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: Lifetimes of the molecules in the excited states are often measured by using pulsed radiation source of duration nearly in the nano second range. If the radiation source has the duration of 2 ns and the number of photons emitted during the pulse source is \(2.5 \times 10^{15}\), calculate the energy of the source.

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: The longest wavelength doublet absorption transition is observed at 589 and 589.6 nm. Calcualte the frequency of each transition and energy difference between two excited states.
_note: The book prints 'Calcualte' for 'Calculate'. Transcribed as printed.

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: The work function for caesium atom is 1.9 eV. Calculate (a) the threshold wavelength and (b) the threshold frequency of the radiation. If the caesium element is irradiated with a wavelength 500 nm, calculate the kinetic energy and the velocity of the ejected photoelectron.

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem:
Following results are observed when sodium metal is irradiated with different wavelengths. Calculate (a) threshold wavelength and, (b) Planck's constant.

| \(\lambda\) (nm) | 500 | 450 | 400 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(v \times 10^{-5}\) (\(\text{cm s}^{-1}\)) | 2.55 | 4.35 | 5.35 |

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: The ejection of the photoelectron from the silver metal in the photoelectric effect experiment can be stopped by applying the voltage of 0.35 V when the radiation 256.7 nm is used. Calculate the work function for silver metal.

subtopic: Developments Leading to the Bohr’s Model of Atom
stem: If the photon of the wavelength 150 pm strikes an atom and one of tis inner bound electrons is ejected out with a velocity of \(1.5 \times 10^{7}\,\text{m s}^{-1}\), calculate the energy with which it is bound to the nucleus.
_note: The book prints 'one of tis inner bound electrons' for 'one of its inner bound electrons'. Transcribed as printed.

subtopic: Bohr’s Model for Hydrogen Atom
stem:
Emission transitions in the Paschen series end at orbit \(n = 3\) and start from orbit \(n\) and can be represeted as \(\nu = 3.29 \times 10^{15}\,(\text{Hz})\,[1/3^2 - 1/n^2]\)

Calculate the value of \(n\) if the transition is observed at 1285 nm. Find the region of the spectrum.
_note: The book prints 'represeted' for 'represented'. Transcribed as printed.

subtopic: Bohr’s Model for Hydrogen Atom
stem: Calculate the wavelength for the emission transition if it starts from the orbit having radius 1.3225 nm and ends at 211.6 pm. Name the series to which this transition belongs and the region of the spectrum.

subtopic: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
stem: Dual behaviour of matter proposed by de Broglie led to the discovery of electron microscope often used for the highly magnified images of biological molecules and other type of material. If the velocity of the electron in this microscope is \(1.6 \times 10^{6}\,\text{ms}^{-1}\), calculate de Broglie wavelength associated with this electron.

subtopic: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
stem: Similar to electron diffraction, neutron diffraction microscope is also used for the determination of the structure of molecules. If the wavelength used here is 800 pm, calculate the characteristic velocity associated with the neutron.

subtopic: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
stem: If the velocity of the electron in Bohr's first orbit is \(2.19 \times 10^{6}\,\text{ms}^{-1}\), calculate the de Broglie wavelength associated with it.

subtopic: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
stem: The velocity associated with a proton moving in a potential difference of 1000 V is \(4.37 \times 10^{5}\,\text{ms}^{-1}\). If the hockey ball of mass 0.1 kg is moving with this velocity, calcualte the wavelength associated with this velocity.
_note: The book prints 'calcualte' for 'calculate'. Transcribed as printed.

subtopic: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model of the Atom
stem: If the position of the electron is measured within an accuracy of \(\pm 0.002\,\text{nm}\), calculate the uncertainty in the momentum of the electron. Suppose the momentum of the electron is \(h/4\pi_m \times 0.05\,\text{nm}\), is there any problem in defining this value.
_note: The printed page sets the second expression with an 'm' subscripted to pi — 'h/4π_m × 0.05 nm' — and closes the sentence with a full stop rather than a question mark. Both left as printed; the oddity of the expression is arguably part of what the question asks about.

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem:
The quantum numbers of six electrons are given below. Arrange them in order of increasing energies. If any of these combination(s) has/have the same energy lists:

1. \(n = 4\), \(l = 2\), \(m_l = -2\), \(m_s = -1/2\)

2. \(n = 3\), \(l = 2\), \(m_l = 1\), \(m_s = +1/2\)

3. \(n = 4\), \(l = 1\), \(m_l = 0\), \(m_s = +1/2\)

4. \(n = 3\), \(l = 2\), \(m_l = -2\), \(m_s = -1/2\)

5. \(n = 3\), \(l = 1\), \(m_l = -1\), \(m_s = +1/2\)

6. \(n = 4\), \(l = 1\), \(m_l = 0\), \(m_s = +1/2\)
_note: The list spans a page break — items 1-2 are at the foot of printed p.72 and items 3-6 at the top of p.73.

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem: The bromine atom possesses 35 electrons. It contains 6 electrons in \(2p\) orbital, 6 electrons in \(3p\) orbital and 5 electron in \(4p\) orbital. Which of these electron experiences the lowest effective nuclear charge?

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem: Among the following pairs of orbitals which orbital will experience the larger effective nuclear charge? (i) \(2s\) and \(3s\), (ii) \(4d\) and \(4f\), (iii) \(3d\) and \(3p\).

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem: The unpaired electrons in Al and Si are present in \(3p\) orbital. Which electrons will experience more effective nuclear charge from the nucleus?

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem: Indicate the number of unpaired electrons in : (a) P, (b) Si, (c) Cr, (d) Fe and (e) Kr.

subtopic: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
stem: (a) How many subshells are associated with \(n = 4\)? (b) How many electrons will be present in the subshells having \(m_s\) value of \(-1/2\) for \(n = 4\)?
